APPLIED REASONING — EPITOME

Interpret. Compute. Check. Explain.

Mindscape Epitome uses pretrained neural interpretation together with Mindscape-engineered structured problem routing, specialized computational methods and explicit verification.

The system is designed to preserve the relationship between a question, its interpreted structure, the computation performed and the answer presented.

01 / Interpretation

Local pretrained advice.

Pinned Qwen3-0.6B supplies advisory interpretation. It is a pretrained model used without fitting and is separate from native Mindscape neural experiments.

02 / Computation

Tools with defined contracts.

Mathematical, physical and programming components compute only supported operations. Complex requests may require explicit schemas, quantities and relationships.

03 / Verification

Checks with a stated scope.

Results preserve expressions, units and method provenance. Some symbolic checks share the solver engine; they are not independent mathematical proofs.

Question→Interpret→Compute→Check→Answer

The integration lives entirely under integrations/hybrid. It can be removed without changing native entrypoints, training, checkpoints or the original architecture.

Neural Interpretation

Interpret supported questions using a local pretrained neural backbone.

Structured Representation

Map supported problems to defined computational tasks and parameters.

Domain Computation

Apply mathematical, physical and programming operations.

Verification

Check supported results and record their verification scope.

Contextual Explanation

Build follow-up explanations from previously verified results.

Feature branch / Context

A checked result
anchors the follow-up.

Follow-ups bind a conversation identifier and exact prior message pair to a server-produced verified result. Client-written assistant prose cannot establish verification. Missing, edited, expired or mismatched history requests clarification.

The memory-only cache holds at most 32 recent records, expiring after 30 minutes. Explanations preserve the verified answer but carry separate, unverified-prose provenance. They do not rerun the solver or pretrained model.

COGNITIVE ARCHITECTURE

Represent. Reason. Act. Verify.

Mindscape’s native research explores structured states, entities, relationships, events, goals and memory.

Experimental neural models operate within controlled research environments where predictions, execution and outcomes can be measured.

Architecture · Research recordCurrent architecture ↗

From input to an observed path.

Mindscape represents a task through the things involved (entities), their connections (relationships), and their current condition (state). A learned policy uses the available representation to propose an allowed action. The system executes it, records what changed, and independently checks the result. Making these concepts explicit helps us inspect the process; it does not by itself prove that the model has learned the underlying concept.

V3 connects three specialists through a shared typed kernel: neural mathematical transitions, Qwen-based Python repair and object-centric physical dynamics. Each domain keeps its own representation, learned model, executor and independent scorer. A shared interface does not by itself imply shared learned knowledge.

Methods
One cognitive cycle. Explicit execution modes.
The R5 kernel records public state, proposed action, original prediction, actual execution, independent verification and ordered trace hashes. Routing is procedural. Tool execution and learned predictions are separately labeled; a failed neural answer is never silently replaced by a reference answer.
Unified kernel report ↗ · Browse the versioned research library ↗
The kernel follows OBSERVE → REPRESENT → PROPOSE → PREDICT → ACT → VERIFY → UPDATE. Typed observations and goals enter the system; predictions describe hypothetical transitions; independent execution records actual outcomes. Evaluation episodes do not update training memory or model weights.

Mathematics
Default R5 mathematics uses bounded Python/SymPy tools with independent checks. Experimental neural arithmetic preserves the fixed R5.2 checkpoint and its unsuccessful claims. Exact symbolic answers do not count as neural learning.
A compact learned model predicts local operations, numerical claims, carry/borrow quantities and next-state values. Declared digit/sign scheduling composes the claims. The executor writes those values without arithmetic correction; an independent arithmetic verifier scores the completed result. Both preserved integration examples fail because of incorrect neural claims.
Python debugging
Pinned Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B receives visible code, contracts, static relationships and approved training experiences. A learned evaluator ranks repair proposals using estimated usefulness and cost. Trusted tools apply validated edits; generated code runs in WASI. Private terminal tests remain outside generation and memory updates.
Physical dynamics
Default R5 forecasting uses approximate analytical contacts and springs, with intervals labeled uncalibrated. Experimental neural mode exposes the fixed R5.3 structured checkpoint and its uncertainty. Pymunk execution is separate from prediction.
The V3.1 candidate uses object-centric states, permutation-consistent pairwise interactions and multi-step supervision. A bounded planner scores action candidates with the learned model, then the simulator executes the selected action. Hidden simulator parameters and future states are excluded from model observations. Finite-rollout stability improved, while the matched-improvement and calibration gates failed.
Shared transition model and provenance
The experimental 6,967-parameter graph model uses domain-specific encoders and heads around a shared message-passing core. R5.1 did not establish transfer: mathematics and physics regressed in every seed, and shared versus target-only training had different target-update exposure. One neural asset slot, strict checkpoint shapes and hashes bind model provenance.
Memory, routing and measured outcomes
Persistent experiences are restricted to approved training evidence. Hypothetical plans remain separate from verified outcomes. Mathematics and physics macro routing submits specialist proposals deterministically; it does not choose semantic answers for the learner. The shared runtime does not pool learned knowledge between domains.
In the preserved V3 demonstration, four recorded requests agree between direct specialists and the kernel: mathematics 0/2, coding 1/1, physics 1/1. These are integration demonstrations, not domain accuracy estimates. Read the integration report ↗

Observation boundaries
A trace is evidence. It does not, by itself, explain why a model produced an output. The recorded diagnostics capture selected paths through a specific implementation.
  • Exact generate arguments, direct forward token IDs, logits, shapes, component invocations, and environment transitions were captured for the selected live diagnostics.
  • Probabilities are derived, uncalibrated softmax summaries. Activation and probability visualizations do not establish causal explanations.
  • Historical coding prompts and logits were not retained and cannot be reconstructed as direct observations.
  • Hidden activations and live coverage of every historical adapter remain unmeasured.
  • Numeric hidden summaries are explicitly reconstructed from observed features and weights.
  • Causal claims are limited to declared controlled software interventions.
Read computation tracing and its limits ↗
Ablations and interventions
To test a component, keep the control fixed. The numeric factorial study manipulated legal-action masking, state-feature readout, and previous-action readout at fixed trained weights. Readout removal does not remove the entire memory module.
The subsequent zero-weight control tested whether trained neural information was necessary with the controller enabled. Verification, environments, and action budgets remained fixed. All unsuccessful outcomes were retained.
Observation and intervention answer different questions.
A diagnostic records what occurred. A controlled intervention tests how a declared change affects outcomes under fixed conditions. Neither supports claims beyond its measured scope.
Current studies retain these controls and add information-matched mathematical comparisons, coding component ablations, and physics stability/calibration gates. Explicit concepts have not established the intended advantage. The next work should test specific failure hypotheses on fresh development evidence before scaling.
